solution:
We have, \(5x - 3 < 3x + 1\)

or \(5x - 3 + 3 < 3x + 1 + 3\) (Rule 1)

or \(5x < 3x + 4\)

subtopic: Algebraic Solutions of Linear Inequalities in One Variable
solution:
We have, \(5x - 3 < 3x + 1\)

or \(5x - 3 + 3 < 3x + 1 + 3\) (Rule 1)

or \(5x < 3x + 4\)

or \(5x - 3x < 3x + 4 - 3x\) (Rule 1)

or \(2x < 4\)

or \(x < 2\) (Rule 2)

When \(x\) is a real number, the solutions of the inequality are given by \(x < 2\), i.e., all real numbers \(x\) which are less than 2. Therefore, the solution set of the inequality is \(x \in (-\infty, 2)\).

subtopic: Algebraic Solutions of Linear Inequalities in One Variable
solution:
We have, \(4x + 3 < 6x + 7\)

or \(4x - 6x < 6x + 4 - 6x\)

or \(-2x < 4\) or \(x > -2\)

i.e., all the real numbers which are greater than \(-2\), are the solutions of the given inequality. Hence, the solution set is \((-2, \infty)\).

subtopic: Algebraic Solutions of Linear Inequalities in One Variable
solution:
We have \(\dfrac{5 - 2x}{3} \le \dfrac{x}{6} - 5\)

or \(2(5 - 2x) \le x - 30\).

or \(10 - 4x \le x - 30\)

or \(-5x \le -40\), i.e., \(x \ge 8\)

Thus, all real numbers \(x\) which are greater than or equal to 8 are the solutions of the given inequality, i.e., \(x \in [8, \infty)\).

stem: Solve \(\dfrac{3x - 4}{2} \ge \dfrac{x + 1}{4} - 1\). Show the graph of the solutions on number line.
solution:
We have

\(\dfrac{3x - 4}{2} \ge \dfrac{x + 1}{4} - 1\)

or \(\dfrac{3x - 4}{2} \ge \dfrac{x - 3}{4}\)

or \(2(3x - 4) \ge (x - 3)\)

or \(6x - 8 \ge x - 3\)

or \(5x \ge 5\) or \(x \ge 1\)

The graphical representation of solutions is given in Fig 5.2: on the number line a dark circle is put at 1 and the line is darkened to the right of 1.

subtopic: Inequalities
stem: The marks obtained by a student of Class XI in first and second terminal examination are 62 and 48, respectively. Find the minimum marks he should get in the annual examination to have an average of at least 60 marks.
solution:
Let \(x\) be the marks obtained by student in the annual examination. Then

\(\dfrac{62 + 48 + x}{3} \ge 60\)

or \(110 + x \ge 180\)

or \(x \ge 70\)

Thus, the student must obtain a minimum of 70 marks to get an average of at least 60 marks.

stem: Find all pairs of consecutive odd natural numbers, both of which are larger than 10, such that their sum is less than 40.
solution:
Let \(x\) be the smaller of the two consecutive odd natural number, so that the other one is \(x + 2\). Then, we should have

\(x > 10\) ... (1)

and \(x + (x + 2) < 40\) ... (2)

Solving (2), we get

\(2x + 2 < 40\)

i.e., \(x < 19\) ... (3)

From (1) and (3), we get

\(10 < x < 19\)

Since \(x\) is an odd number, \(x\) can take the values 11, 13, 15, and 17. So, the required possible pairs will be

\((11, 13), (13, 15), (15, 17), (17, 19)\)

stem:
A man wants to cut three lengths from a single piece of board of length 91cm. The second length is to be 3cm longer than the shortest and the third length is to be twice as long as the shortest. What are the possible lengths of the shortest board if the third piece is to be at least 5cm longer than the second?

[Hint: If \(x\) is the length of the shortest board, then \(x\), \((x + 3)\) and \(2x\) are the lengths of the second and third piece, respectively. Thus, \(x + (x + 3) + 2x \le 91\) and \(2x \ge (x + 3) + 5\)].
_note: Book slip in the printed Hint, transcribed verbatim: it lists THREE expressions \(x\), \((x + 3)\) and \(2x\) but attributes them to only "the second and third piece". \(x\) is the shortest board (as the Hint's own opening clause states), so the list should read "the shortest, second and third piece". The two inequalities that follow are correct and unaffected.

subtopic: Algebraic Solutions of Linear Inequalities in One Variable
stem:
Solve the system of inequalities:

\(3x - 7 < 5 + x\) ... (1)

\(11 - 5x \le 1\) ... (2)

and represent the solutions on the number line.
solution:
From inequality (1), we have

\(3x - 7 < 5 + x\)

or \(x < 6\) ... (3)

Also, from inequality (2), we have

\(11 - 5x \le 1\)

or \(-5x \le -10\) i.e., \(x \ge 2\) ... (4)

If we draw the graph of inequalities (3) and (4) on the number line, we see that the values of \(x\), which are common to both, are shown by bold line in Fig 5.3 (a dark circle at 2, an open circle at 6, and the segment between them darkened).

Thus, solution of the system are real numbers \(x\) lying between 2 and 6 including 2, i.e.,

\(2 \le x < 6\)

subtopic: Inequalities
stem: In an experiment, a solution of hydrochloric acid is to be kept between \(30^\circ\) and \(35^\circ\) Celsius. What is the range of temperature in degree Fahrenheit if conversion formula is given by \(\text{C} = \dfrac{5}{9}(\text{F} - 32)\), where C and F represent temperature in degree Celsius and degree Fahrenheit, respectively.
solution:
It is given that \(30 < \text{C} < 35\).

Putting \(\text{C} = \dfrac{5}{9}(\text{F} - 32)\), we get

\(30 < \dfrac{5}{9}(\text{F} - 32) < 35\),

or \(\dfrac{9}{5} \times (30) < (\text{F} - 32) < \dfrac{9}{5} \times (35)\)

or \(54 < (\text{F} - 32) < 63\)

or \(86 < \text{F} < 95\).

Thus, the required range of temperature is between \(86^\circ\ \text{F}\) and \(95^\circ\ \text{F}\).

subtopic: Inequalities
stem: A manufacturer has 600 litres of a 12% solution of acid. How many litres of a 30% acid solution must be added to it so that acid content in the resulting mixture will be more than 15% but less than 18%?
solution:
Let \(x\) litres of 30% acid solution is required to be added. Then

Total mixture \(= (x + 600)\) litres

Therefore \(30\%\, x + 12\%\) of \(600 > 15\%\) of \((x + 600)\)

and \(30\%\, x + 12\%\) of \(600 < 18\%\) of \((x + 600)\)

or \(\dfrac{30x}{100} + \dfrac{12}{100}(600) > \dfrac{15}{100}(x + 600)\)

and \(\dfrac{30x}{100} + \dfrac{12}{100}(600) < \dfrac{18}{100}(x + 600)\)

or \(30x + 7200 > 15x + 9000\)

and \(30x + 7200 < 18x + 10800\)

or \(15x > 1800\) and \(12x < 3600\)

or \(x > 120\) and \(x < 300\),

i.e. \(120 < x < 300\)

Thus, the number of litres of the 30% solution of acid will have to be more than 120 litres but less than 300 litres.
